questions.stem: Parents lend $2,000,000 to their child to start a business. The loan is interest-free and is payable on demand. The imputed interest is subject to

choices.label: A
choices.text: The gift tax only in the year the parents lend the money.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The generation-skipping transfer tax, but not the gift tax.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The gift tax each year the loan is outstanding.

questions.explanation:
The Internal Revenue Code (IRC) generally treats an interest-free loan to a family member as a gift loan. A gift loan is any type of loan that charges no interest or a below-market interest rate where the intent of the lender (parents) is that the imputed interest that is not charged is a gift to the borrower (a child).

Under the IRC rules, the forgone interest is treated as interest income. The transfer is deemed to occur on the last day of the calendar year for each year the loan is outstanding. Therefore, gift tax may apply to the amount of forgone interest each year the loan is still outstanding.

("The gift tax only in the year the parents lend the money.") This deemed transfer applies to every year the loan is outstanding, not just the year the loan was made.

("The generation-skipping transfer tax, but not the gift tax.") The generation-skipping transfer tax would apply if the loan had been made to a grandchild, rather than the child, of the lenders.

("An excise tax.") Excise taxes are imposed by the federal government on specific types of goods or services.
questions.explanationJa: 家族への無利子貸付は贈与貸付（gift loan）として扱われ、本来課されるべき利子（imputed interest）は貸し手から借り手への贈与とみなされる。この擬制的な移転は貸付が残っている各年の12月31日に生じたものとされるため、贈与税は貸付を行った年だけでなく、貸付が残っている毎年の免除利子に対して課される可能性がある。世代跳躍移転税は孫に貸し付けた場合に問題となるもので、子への貸付には関係しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.1

questions.stem: Husband and wife, U.S. citizens, were married for the entire Year 1 calendar year. In Year 1, the husband gave a $60,000 cash gift to his sister. The husband and wife made no other gifts in Year 1. They each signed a timely election to treat the $60,000 gift as one made by each spouse. Assume that the gift tax annual exclusion is $15,000. Disregarding the unified credit and estate tax consequences, what amount of the Year 1 gift is taxable to the husband and wife for gift tax purposes?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the gift-splitting election for the husband's $60,000 gift to his sister treats the gift as being given one-half ($30,000) from each spouse. Each spouse's annual exclusion of $15,000 is subtracted from his or her gift, leaving a taxable gift of $15,000 from each spouse and total taxable gift of $30,000.

Husband | Wife
Half of original gift | $30,000 | $30,000
Annual exclusion | (15,000) | (15,000)
Taxable gift | $15,000 | $15,000
questions.explanationJa: 贈与分割（gift-splitting）を選択すると、夫の妹への$60,000の贈与は夫婦それぞれが半額の$30,000ずつ贈与したものとして扱われる。各配偶者は自分の贈与から年間除外額$15,000を差し引くので、課税贈与額はそれぞれ$15,000となる。したがって夫婦合計の課税贈与額は$30,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.2

questions.stem: An individual taxpayer makes the following gifts during the year: a residence to his married son; a life estate in a trust to his older daughter; and a remainder interest in the trust for his younger daughter. In addition, the taxpayer makes a cash contribution to a qualified charity. Which of the gifts qualifies for neither a deduction nor an exclusion in determining the taxpayer's gift tax for the year?
questions.explanation:
A gift of a future interest must be reported, regardless of size, at the present value of the future interest. A future interest is anything that is not immediately available to be enjoyed by the gift beneficiary. In this scenario, the remainder interest can't be used by the younger daughter until the older daughter's life estate expires. Therefore, the remainder interest is considered to be a gift of a future interest. As such, it is subject to gift tax and qualifies for neither the gift deduction nor the annual exclusion amount.

("The residence." / "The life estate in trust.") Gifts of a present interest are subject to gift taxes for the year the taxpayer transfers the property to the recipient. The amount equals the value of the present interest less deductions and the annual exclusion. Both the gift of the residence to the son and the life estate to the older daughter are present interests because those gift beneficiaries were able to enjoy the gift immediately upon receipt.

("The cash contribution.") Charitable contributions are not considered gifts.
questions.explanationJa: 将来権（future interest）の贈与は、受贈者がすぐには享受できない権利の贈与であり、金額にかかわらず現在価値で報告しなければならず、年間除外額の対象にもならない。年下の娘の残余権は、年上の娘の生涯権が終わるまで使えないため将来権にあたり、控除も除外も受けられない。息子への住宅と年上の娘の生涯権は直ちに享受できる現在権なので年間除外の対象となり、適格慈善団体への現金寄附は課税対象の贈与として扱われない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.3

questions.stem: Steve and Kay Briar, U.S. citizens, were married for the entire Year 4 calendar year. In Year 4, Steve gave a $40,000 cash gift to his sister. The Briars made no other gifts in Year 4. They each signed a timely election to treat the $40,000 gift as made one-half by each spouse. Assume that the gift tax annual exclusion is $15,000. Disregarding the unified credit and estate tax consequences, what amount of the Year 4 gift is taxable to the Briars?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, the gift-splitting election for Steve's $40,000 gift to his sister treats the gift as being given one-half ($20,000) from each spouse. Each spouse's annual exclusion of $15,000 is subtracted from their gift, leaving a taxable gift of $5,000 from each spouse and total taxable gift of $10,000.
questions.explanationJa: 贈与分割を選択すると、Steveの妹への$40,000の贈与は夫婦がそれぞれ半額の$20,000ずつ贈与したものとして扱われる。各配偶者の贈与から年間除外額$15,000を差し引くと、課税贈与額はそれぞれ$5,000となる。したがって夫婦合計の課税贈与額は$10,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.4

questions.stem: An organization exempt from tax under Internal Revenue Code Section 501(c)(3) is considering buying stock in an S corporation engaged in an unrelated business. Which of the following statements is correct regarding this investment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: S corporation distributions will be taxed to the organization at a flat 35% rate.

choices.label: B
choices.text: S corporation ordinary business income will be taxed to the organization as unrelated business income at regular corporate rates.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The S corporation will be required to file for tax-exempt status.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The S corporation will be deemed a tax-exempt organization.

questions.explanation:
A nonprofit organization isn't taxed on income derived from activities directly related to performing its purpose (eg, charity, religion, education). However, the organization may receive unrelated business income (UBI)--trade or business income not associated with its tax-exempt purpose that is earned on a regular basis (income from S corporations). UBI results in income taxes (assessed at the corporate rate) if the sum of the separately calculated unrelated business taxable income (UBI) exceeds $1,000.

For example, an exempt organization whose purpose is to prevent cruelty to animals receives UBI from selling pet supplies or providing grooming services to the general public. Although investment income is generally excluded from UBI, any income from an S corporation is considered trade or business income and is treated as UBI income.

("S corporation distributions will be taxed to the organization at a fl…") Distributions from an S corporation are a return of capital and therefore nontaxable to the extent of stock basis. If the UBI tax applies, it is assessed at the corporate tax rate (not a flat 35%).

("The S corporation will be required to file for tax-exempt status." / "The S corporation will be deemed a tax-exempt organization.") The purchase of S corporation stock by a nonprofit organization has no effect on the exemption status of the S corporation.
questions.explanationJa: 免税団体は免税目的に直接関係する活動の所得には課税されないが、免税目的と無関係で継続的に営まれる事業の所得（UBI）があり、それが$1,000を超えると法人税率で課税される。投資所得は通常UBIから除かれるが、S corporationから配分される所得はすべて事業所得としてUBIに該当するため、通常の法人税率で課税される。S corporationからの分配は株式の取得原価の範囲で元本の回収として非課税であり、一律35%で課税されるわけではない。また免税団体が株式を買っても、S corporation自体の免税資格には影響しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.5

questions.stem: Which of the following payments would require the donor to file a gift tax return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $30,000 to a university for a spouse's tuition.

choices.label: B
choices.text: $40,000 to a university for a cousin's room and board.

choices.label: C
choices.text: $50,000 to a hospital for a parent's medical expenses.

choices.label: D
choices.text: $80,000 to a physician for a friend's surgery.

questions.explanation:
When a donor makes a gift to any one person and that gift exceeds the annual exclusion amount, the donor must file a gift tax return (Form 709) for the year in which the gift was made. However, certain transfers are excluded from gift tax treatment. For example, payments on behalf of another party for medical expenses or tuition that are made directly to the provider are not treated as taxable gifts.

The educational exclusion applies for tuition only. Educational expenses such as room and board, when paid on behalf of another party, are considered taxable gifts even if paid to the provider. The donor must file a gift tax return if the amount of the nonexcludable education payment exceeds the annual exclusion amount.
questions.explanationJa: 同一人への贈与が年間除外額を超える場合、贈与者はその年の贈与税申告書（Form 709）を提出しなければならない。ただし、他人のための医療費や授業料を提供者に直接支払った場合は課税贈与として扱われない。教育に関する除外は授業料に限られ、寮費・食費（room and board）は提供者に直接支払っても課税贈与となる。したがって、いとこの寮費・食費として大学に支払った$40,000は年間除外額を超えるため申告が必要になる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.6

questions.stem: During Year 4, Alex, a single taxpayer, gave cash of $7,200 to Campbell, $15,000 to Jackie, and $34,000 to Robin. Assume a $15,000 annual exclusion amount. In calculating taxable gifts for the Year 4 gift tax return, Alex may subtract an annual exclusion amount of:
questions.explanation:
In this scenario Alex's annual exclusion amount for Year 4 is:

Gift to Campbell | $7,200 | Lesser of $7,200 or $15,000 annual exclusion
Gift to Jackie | 15,000 | Gift amount equals annual exclusion amount
Gift to Robin | 15,000 | Lesser of $34,000 or $15,000 annual exclusion

Total exclusion $37,200
questions.explanationJa: 年間除外額は受贈者1人ごとに、贈与額と除外額のいずれか少ない額を差し引く。Campbellへの$7,200は全額、Jackieへの$15,000も全額、Robinへの$34,000は上限の$15,000が除外される。したがって差し引ける年間除外額の合計は$37,200（$7,200＋$15,000＋$15,000）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.7

questions.stem: Which of the following is an attribute of a complex trust?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It distributes income to more than one beneficiary.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It has a grantor that is not an individual.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It has a beneficiary that is not an individual.

questions.explanation:
Typically, a trust is established for the purpose of benefiting specific individuals or charities without giving the beneficiary(s) current control of the trust's principal (corpus). For federal income tax purposes, there are three types of trusts: grantor, simple, and complex. Grantor trusts are not taxed as separate entities by the IRS. Simple and complex trusts are taxed as separate entities that report income on Form 1041.

Under IRC rules, if a trust does not meet the requirements to be a simple trust, it is classified as a complex trust. A complex trust does or can:

make annual beneficiary distributions that are below the trust's distributable net income,

make distributions to a charity, and

distribute principal (corpus).

("It distributes income to more than one beneficiary." / "It has a grantor that is not an individual." / "It has a beneficiary that is not an individual.") Trusts can be established by an individual or an entity (corporation) for the benefit of one or more beneficiaries. A beneficiary can be an individual or any type of organization (charity, government). However, these options are not relevant in determining whether a trust is classified as complex or simple for federal income tax purposes.

Note:
A complex trust is one that does or can do any of the following: (1) make annual beneficiary distributions that are below the trust's distributable net income, (2) make distributions to a charity, and (3) distribute principal (corpus).
questions.explanationJa: 連邦所得税上の信託には、グランター信託、単純信託（simple trust）、複合信託（complex trust）があり、単純信託の要件を満たさない信託は複合信託となる。複合信託は、分配可能純所得（DNI）を下回る分配、慈善団体への分配、元本（corpus）の分配を行う、または行うことができる信託である。したがって元本を分配することが複合信託の特徴である。複数の受益者への分配や、委託者・受益者が個人でないことは、単純信託か複合信託かの判定には関係しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.8

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of a revocable trust?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The trust is excluded from the gross estate of the transferor.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The transferor retains the power to terminate the trust.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The income of the trust is taxed to the trust.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A taxable gift occurs on the creation of the trust.

questions.explanation:
There are two categories of trusts: revocable and irrevocable. In a revocable trust, the grantor retains control over--and claim to--the assets transferred. Therefore, the grantor may make changes or even terminate the trust up to the date of the grantor's death.

In contrast, an irrevocable trust treats the transfer of assets as permanent, and the grantor has no control over or claim to the assets transferred. Upon the grantor's death, a revocable trust becomes irrevocable, and the assets pass to the beneficiaries.

("The trust is excluded from the gross estate of the transferor." / "The income of the trust is taxed to the trust.") Because the grantor retains the right to alter or terminate a revocable trust, the trust assets are considered property still owned by the grantor. Accordingly, income generated from the trust is taxable to the grantor, and the trust assets are included in the grantor's estate.

("A taxable gift occurs on the creation of the trust.") A taxable gift occurs when a grantor transfers assets to an irrevocable trust--not a revocable trust--and the grantor is liable for any resulting gift taxes.
questions.explanationJa: 撤回可能信託（revocable trust）では、委託者が移転した資産の支配権と請求権を保持しており、死亡するまで信託の変更や終了ができる。委託者が終了させる権限を持つため、信託財産は依然として委託者の所有とみなされる。その結果、信託の所得は信託ではなく委託者に課税され、信託財産は委託者の遺産に含まれる。課税贈与が生じるのは撤回不能信託に資産を移転したときであり、撤回可能信託の設定時には生じない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.9

questions.stem:
This year, Jordan, a single taxpayer, gave $35,000 cash to Alex. Alex used the money to pay medical expenses. Jordan also paid $16,000 in tuition expenses directly to Alex's university on Alex's behalf. Assume the annual gift tax exclusion is $15,000, the gift tax rate is 20%, and Jordan has not used any of the unified credit.

What is Jordan's taxable gift amount and the lowest possible gift tax owed for this year, if any?
Taxable gift | Gift tax owed
questions.explanation:
However, even if there is an amount subject to gift taxation after the exclusions, the taxpayer may not owe gift tax because of the unified transfer tax credit against gift and estate taxes. The unified credit applies over a taxpayer's lifetime to both gift and estate taxes. The large credit effectively makes a taxpayer's cumulative wealth transfer tax free for a substantial amount of wealth transfers ($13 millions).

In this scenario, Jordan's taxable gift and lowest possible tax owed are:

Gross gifts ($35,000 + $16,000 tuition payment): $51,000
Exclusion for tuition: (16,000)
Annual exclusion per donee: (15,000)
Net taxable gifts: $20,000
Tentative gift tax ($20,000 × 20%): $4,000
Unified credit based on lifetime exemption amount: (4,000)
Gift tax due and owed: $0

Note: The taxpayer will have $20,000 less of the unified credit exemption to use in the future.
questions.explanationJa: Alexに現金で渡した$35,000は、医療費に使われたとしても医療提供者に直接支払ったものではないため医療費の除外の対象にならない。一方、大学へ直接支払った授業料$16,000は除外される。贈与総額$51,000から授業料$16,000と年間除外額$15,000を差し引いた$20,000が課税贈与額となる。仮の贈与税は$4,000（$20,000×20%）だが、生涯にわたり贈与税と遺産税に共通で使える統一税額控除で相殺されるため、納付額は$0となる（その分、将来使える控除枠が減る）。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.10

questions.stem: A taxpayer purchases and is the owner of an insurance contract on his own life and designates his two children as equal beneficiaries. The taxpayer makes all the premium payments. How many gifts of property, if any, have been made for gift tax purposes?
questions.explanation:
There are three types of lifetime transfers; only two are considered gifts of property for gift tax purposes.

Present interest: A gift of a present interest is a current transfer of wealth that can be accessed by the recipient immediately (transfer of cash). Gifts of a present interest are considered gifts for gift tax purposes.

Future interest: A gift of a future interest is an irrevocable right to access wealth at a future time. The most common example is transferring property to an irrevocable trust and instructing the trustee to distribute the property when the beneficiary reaches a certain age. Gifts of a future interest are considered gifts for gift tax purposes.

Incomplete gift: A gift is incomplete when it is a revocable transfer of the right to access wealth at a future time. An incomplete gift is not considered a gift for gift tax purposes.

In this scenario, the parent retained ownership of the insurance policy and paid the premiums. As a result, the parent retained the right to revoke the future benefits to the children because he can cancel the policy at any time. The gift is incomplete; therefore, no gifts are considered to have been made for gift tax purposes
questions.explanationJa: 贈与税上の贈与となるのは、直ちに享受できる現在権の贈与と、将来享受する撤回不能な権利である将来権の贈与であり、撤回可能な移転は不完全な贈与として贈与にあたらない。本問の納税者は保険契約の所有者のまま保険料を支払っており、いつでも契約を解約して子への将来の給付を取り消せる。したがって贈与は不完全であり、贈与税上の贈与は0件である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.11

questions.stem: Pat created a trust, transferred property to this trust, and retained certain interests. For income tax purposes, Pat was treated as the owner of the trust. Pat has created which of the following types of trusts?
questions.explanation:
There are two categories of trusts: grantor (revocable) and irrevocable. In a grantor trust, the grantor retains control over (retains interests in) the assets transferred to the trust. Retained interests include the grantor's right to make changes or even terminate the trust up to the date of the grantor's death. In this scenario, since Pat (the grantor) retains certain interests in the trust assets, the trust is a grantor trust (revocable trust).

Grantor trusts are not taxed as separate entities by the IRS because the trust assets are considered to be still owned by the grantor. The trust income is taxable to the grantor as long as the grantor retains an interest in the trust assets.

In contrast, an irrevocable trust treats the transfer of assets to the trust as permanent, and the grantor has no control over or claim to the assets transferred. IRS rules classify irrevocable trusts as either simple or complex. Irrevocable trusts are taxed as separate entities that report income on Form 1041.

("Pre-need funeral.") A preneed funeral agreement is not a type of trust.
questions.explanationJa: グランター信託では、委託者が信託に移転した資産に対する支配権（信託の変更や終了の権利など）を保持する。Patは一定の権利を保持し、所得税上も信託の所有者として扱われているので、グランター信託を設定したことになる。グランター信託は独立した課税主体とされず、所得は委託者に課税される。単純信託と複合信託は、委託者が支配権を持たない撤回不能信託の区分であり、葬儀の事前契約はそもそも信託の種類ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.12

questions.stem: Which of the following transactions is subject to the gift tax before the gift tax annual exclusion is taken into account?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Contribution of cash to a candidate for the U.S. Senate.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Transfer to a trust for the benefit of relatives where the donor determines the amount of distributions to be made.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reimbursement to a grandchild for medical school tuition.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Naming of a new beneficiary on an insured's life insurance policy.

questions.explanation:
Gifts of a present interest are subject to gift taxes for the year the taxpayer transfers the property to the recipient. Any amount of the gift over the annual exclusion is subject to gift taxes.

A gift given directly to a grandchild as reimbursement for tuition is a taxable gift of a present interest. It is subject to gift taxes before the gift tax annual exclusion is considered. Had the grandparent paid the tuition directly to the medical school, the payment would not have been a taxable gift. In addition to direct tuition payments, certain other gifts are excluded from gift tax, including transfers to a spouse, charitable contributions, and political contributions.

("Transfer to a trust for the benefit of relatives where the donor dete…" / "Naming of a new beneficiary on an insured's life insurance policy.") A transfer to a trust where the donor can determine the amounts paid to relatives and changing the beneficiary on a life insurance policy are both incomplete transfers. Nothing has been given yet because the trust donor can determine the amount, if any, paid to relatives and the insured can select a different beneficiary in the future. Therefore, they are not subject to gift tax.
questions.explanationJa: 現在権の贈与は財産を移転した年の贈与税の対象となり、年間除外額を超える部分が課税される。孫に医学部の授業料を払い戻す形で渡した現金は現在権の贈与であり、年間除外を考慮する前の段階で贈与税の対象となる。祖父母が授業料を学校に直接支払っていれば、課税贈与にはならなかった。分配額を贈与者が決められる信託への移転と、生命保険の受取人の変更は、いずれも将来変更できる不完全な移転なので贈与税の対象にならず、政治献金も贈与税の対象外である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.13

questions.stem: Brown transfers property to a trust. A local bank was named trustee. Brown retained no powers over the trust. The trust instrument provides that current income and $6,000 of principal must be distributed annually to the beneficiary. What type of trust was created?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC rules, if a trust does not meet the requirements to be a simple trust, it is classified as a complex trust. A complex trust does or can:

make annual beneficiary distributions that are below the trust's distributable net income,

make distributions to a charity, or

distribute principal (corpus).

("Simple.") In this scenario, the trustee is required to distribute corpus once each year. Therefore, the trust cannot be classified as a simple trust.

("Grantor." / "Revocable.") The trust created by Brown is not a grantor trust (revocable trust) because Brown retained no powers over the trust (power to revoke). Grantor trusts are not taxed as separate entities by the IRS.
questions.explanationJa: 単純信託の要件を満たさない信託は複合信託となり、複合信託はDNIを下回る分配、慈善団体への分配、元本の分配を行う（または行える）信託である。本問の信託は当期の所得に加えて毎年$6,000の元本を分配しなければならないため、単純信託ではなく複合信託となる。Brownは撤回権などの権限を一切保持していないので、グランター信託（撤回可能信託）にもあたらない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.14

questions.stem: The filing of a return covering unrelated business income

choices.label: A
choices.text: Is required of all exempt organizations having at least $1,000 of unrelated business taxable income for the year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Relieves the organization of having to file a separate annual information return.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Is not necessary if all of the organization's income is used exclusively for charitable purposes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Must be accompanied by a minimum payment of 50% of the tax due as shown on the return, with the balance of tax payable six months later.

questions.explanation:
A tax-exempt organization is not taxed on income derived from activities directly related to performing its purpose (charity, religion, education). However, the organization may receive unrelated business income (UBI)--trade or business income not associated with its tax-exempt purpose that is earned on a regular basis.

A tax-exempt organization is required to file a business income tax return if it has UBI of $1,000 or more. Filing the business income tax return does not relieve the organization of obligations to file a separate information return ("Relieves the organization of having to file a separate annual informa…").

("Is not necessary if all of the organization's income is used exclusiv…") The fact that income from an unrelated business is used to support the organization does not automatically exempt that income from UBI taxation.

("Must be accompanied by a minimum payment of 50% of the tax due as sho…") Taxes due on UBI are payable at the time the return is due, and estimated taxes are required if the organization expects its tax for the year to be $500 or more.
questions.explanationJa: 免税団体は、免税目的と無関係な事業の所得（UBI）が$1,000以上ある場合、その所得の申告書を提出しなければならない。この申告書を提出しても、別途の年次情報申告書の提出義務は免除されない。事業所得を団体の慈善目的に使っていても、それだけでUBIへの課税を免れることはない。UBIに係る税は申告期限に納付し、年間の税額が$500以上と見込まれる場合は予定納税が必要であり、半額を先に納め残りを6か月後に納めるという仕組みはない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.15

questions.stem: On January 1, Year 7, a taxpayer created a $300,000 trust that provided his mother with a lifetime income interest starting on January 1, Year 7, with the remainder interest to go to his son. The taxpayer expressly retained the power to revoke both the income interest and the remainder interest at any time. Who will be taxed on the trust's Year 7 income?
questions.explanation: The IRS does not tax revocable trusts as separate entities because the trust assets are still considered to be owned by the grantor. Accordingly, income generated from the revocable trust is taxable to the grantor, and the trust assets are included in the grantor's estate. Neither the trust nor the beneficiaries (mother, son) are taxed on the income of a revocable trust
questions.explanationJa: 撤回可能信託は、信託財産が依然として委託者の所有とみなされるため、独立した課税主体として扱われない。したがって撤回可能信託から生じた所得は委託者に課税され、信託財産も委託者の遺産に含まれる。本問の納税者は所得権と残余権の両方をいつでも撤回できるので、Year 7の信託所得は信託や受益者（母、息子）ではなく納税者本人に課税される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Trusts, Gift Taxes & Tax-Exempt Organizations Q.16

questions.stem: What is the due date of a federal estate tax return (Form 706), for a taxpayer who died on May 15, year 2, assuming that a request for an extension of time is not filed?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §6075(a), the federal estate tax return (Form 706) is due 9 months after the date of the decedent's death. A 6-month extension is available under IRC §6081, but none was requested here.

Date of death: May 15, year 2
Due date: May 15, year 2 + 9 months = February 15, year 3

September 15, year 2 is only 4 months after death. December 31, year 2 is the end of the calendar year, which is irrelevant to the estate tax return. January 31, year 3 is not tied to the 9-month rule.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §6075(a)により、連邦遺産税申告書（Form 706）の期限は死亡日から9か月後。§6081で6か月の延長が可能だが、本問では申請していない。

死亡日 year 2年5月15日 ＋ 9か月 = year 3年2月15日

year 2年9月15日は死亡後4か月にすぎない。year 2年12月31日は暦年末で遺産税申告とは無関係。year 3年1月31日も9か月ルールと結び付かない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.13 (AICPA No. 90213)

questions.stem:
A trust has distributable net income of $14,000 and distributes $20,000 to the sole beneficiary. What amounts are taxable to the trust and to the beneficiary?

Trust | Beneficiary
questions.explanation:
Distributable net income (DNI, IRC §643(a)) caps both the trust's distribution deduction and the amount taxable to the beneficiary. Under IRC §661(a), the trust deducts distributions, but not more than DNI. Under IRC §662(a), the beneficiary includes distributions in income, but not more than DNI. The excess distribution is treated as a tax-free distribution of corpus.

Distributions: $20,000; DNI: $14,000
Trust distribution deduction = lesser of $20,000 or $14,000 = $14,000
Trust taxable income from DNI = $14,000 - $14,000 = $0
Beneficiary's taxable amount = lesser of $20,000 or $14,000 = $14,000

Trust $14,000 / beneficiary $0 ignores the distribution deduction and taxes the income at the trust level even though it was distributed. Trust $14,000 / beneficiary $20,000 taxes the same income twice and taxes the beneficiary beyond DNI. Trust $0 / beneficiary $20,000 taxes the beneficiary on $6,000 of corpus, which exceeds DNI.
questions.explanationJa:
分配可能純所得（DNI、IRC §643(a)）は、信託の分配控除と受益者の課税額の両方の上限となる。§661(a)により信託は分配額をDNIを上限に控除し、§662(a)により受益者は分配額をDNIを上限に所得に含める。DNIを超える分配は元本の非課税分配となる。

分配額 $20,000、DNI $14,000
信託の分配控除 = $20,000と$14,000の小さい方 = $14,000
信託の課税所得 = $14,000 − $14,000 = $0
受益者の課税額 = $20,000と$14,000の小さい方 = $14,000

信託$14,000・受益者$0は分配控除を無視している。信託$14,000・受益者$20,000は同じ所得に二重課税し、受益者にもDNI超の課税をしている。信託$0・受益者$20,000はDNIを超える元本$6,000まで受益者に課税している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.39 (AICPA No. 90239)

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of a revocable trust?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The grantor will be subject to gift taxes on the transfer of property to the trust.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The trust assets are subject to being probated upon the death of the grantor.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The grantor loses power to control the trust funds for federal estate tax purposes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The trust is included in the gross estate of the grantor.

questions.explanation:
Because the grantor of a revocable trust retains the power to revoke, amend, or terminate the trust, the trust property is included in the grantor's gross estate at death under IRC §2038. This inclusion is the main tax disadvantage of a revocable trust.

Transfers to a revocable trust are incomplete gifts, so no gift tax is imposed on the transfer. Trust assets pass under the trust instrument and avoid probate, which is a principal advantage of the trust. The grantor keeps control over the trust funds (that retained control is what causes estate inclusion) rather than losing it.
questions.explanationJa:
撤回可能信託の設定者は信託の撤回・変更・終了の権限を保持するため、死亡時に信託財産が総遺産に含まれる（IRC §2038）。これが撤回可能信託の主な税務上の不利益である。

撤回可能信託への移転は未完成贈与なので贈与税は課されない。信託財産は信託証書に従って承継され、検認（probate）を経ないのがむしろ利点である。設定者は信託財産の支配を失わず、その支配を保持していることこそが遺産算入の原因である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.17 (AICPA No. 90817)

questions.stem: A husband and wife agree to split monetary gifts to their relatives. The husband gives his daughter $20,500, and the wife gives her niece $17,000. The annual exclusion is $12,000. What amount is the taxable gift for the husband and wife?
questions.explanation:
When spouses elect gift splitting under IRC §2513, each gift made by either spouse to a third party is treated as made one-half by each spouse. Each spouse then applies the annual exclusion (given as $12,000) separately to each donee.

Gift to daughter: $20,500 → $10,250 treated as made by each spouse
Gift to niece: $17,000 → $8,500 treated as made by each spouse
Each spouse's gift to the daughter: $10,250 − $10,250 exclusion = $0
Each spouse's gift to the niece: $8,500 − $8,500 exclusion = $0
Total taxable gifts: $0

The $13,500 amount applies a single exclusion to each gift without splitting ($20,500 − $12,000 = $8,500 plus $17,000 − $12,000 = $5,000). The $17,000 amount and the $37,500 amount ignore the annual exclusion for one or both gifts.
questions.explanationJa:
配偶者がIRC §2513の贈与分割を選択すると、どちらの配偶者が第三者に贈与しても、各配偶者が半分ずつ贈与したものとして扱われる。各配偶者は受贈者ごとに年間除外額（問題では$12,000）を適用する。

娘への贈与$20,500 → 各配偶者$10,250
姪への贈与$17,000 → 各配偶者$8,500
各配偶者の娘への贈与: $10,250 − 除外$10,250 = $0
各配偶者の姪への贈与: $8,500 − 除外$8,500 = $0
課税贈与額の合計: $0

$13,500は分割せずに各贈与から除外額を1回だけ引いている（$20,500 − $12,000 = $8,500と$17,000 − $12,000 = $5,000）。$17,000や$37,500は一方または両方の贈与で年間除外額を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.30 (AICPA No. 90830)

questions.stem: Mike and Carol, a married couple, have two assets at the time of Mike's death: a $10,000,000 life insurance policy owned by Mike naming Carol as the sole beneficiary, and $8,000,000 of real estate owned by the couple as joint tenants with right of survivorship. What is the amount of the marital deduction to Mike's estate for these two assets?
questions.explanation:
The marital deduction equals the value of property included in the decedent's gross estate that passes to the surviving spouse (IRC §2056).

Life insurance owned by Mike: fully included in the gross estate (§2042) and paid to Carol → $10,000,000
Real estate held by spouses as joint tenants with right of survivorship: one-half included (§2040(b)) and passes to Carol → $8,000,000 × 50% = $4,000,000
Marital deduction: $10,000,000 + $4,000,000 = $14,000,000

The $9,000,000 amount includes only half of the insurance proceeds and half of the real estate. The $10,000,000 amount omits the real estate. The $18,000,000 amount includes all of the real estate, but only one-half of property held jointly by spouses is in the gross estate.
questions.explanationJa:
配偶者控除額は、総遺産に含まれ生存配偶者に移転する財産の価額である（IRC §2056）。

Mikeが所有する生命保険: 全額が総遺産に算入され（§2042）、Carolに支払われる → $10,000,000
夫婦の生存者権付き合有不動産: 半分が算入され（§2040(b)）、Carolに移転 → $8,000,000 × 50% = $4,000,000
配偶者控除: $10,000,000 + $4,000,000 = $14,000,000

$9,000,000は保険金と不動産の両方を半分にしている。$10,000,000は不動産を落としている。$18,000,000は不動産全額を含めているが、夫婦の合有財産は半分しか総遺産に入らない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.32 (AICPA No. 90832)

questions.stem:
Orsen, a U.S. citizen and the sole income beneficiary of a simple trust, is entitled to receive current distributions of the trust income. During the current year the trust reported:

Dividend income | $8,000
Accounting fees allocable to income | (2,000)
Short-term capital gain allocable to corpus | 3,000

What amount of the trust income is includible in Orsen's gross income?
questions.explanation:
A beneficiary of a simple trust includes in gross income the trust income required to be distributed currently, limited to distributable net income (DNI) (IRC §652(a)). Capital gains allocated to corpus are excluded from DNI (§643(a)(3)).

Dividend income: $8,000
Less accounting fees allocable to income: (2,000)
Trust accounting income required to be distributed: $6,000
DNI (short-term capital gain allocated to corpus excluded): $6,000
Amount includible in Orsen's gross income: $6,000

The $0 amount ignores that a simple trust's income is taxed to the beneficiary. The $8,000 amount ignores the fees allocable to income. The $9,000 amount includes the capital gain that is allocated to corpus and retained by the trust.
questions.explanationJa:
単純信託の受益者は、当期に分配すべき信託所得を分配可能純所得（DNI）の範囲で総所得に算入する（IRC §652(a)）。元本に配分された譲渡益はDNIに含まれない（§643(a)(3)）。

配当所得: $8,000
所得に配分される会計報酬: (2,000)
分配すべき信託会計上の所得: $6,000
DNI（元本に配分された短期譲渡益を除く）: $6,000
Orsenの総所得算入額: $6,000

$0は単純信託の所得が受益者に課税されることを無視している。$8,000は所得に配分される報酬を差し引いていない。$9,000は元本に配分され信託に留保される譲渡益まで含めている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2016 Recently Released Q.20 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: At the close of the prior year, an individual taxpayer transferred assets into an irrevocable trust, retaining the right to the income from the trust for life. During the year, the assets earned ordinary dividends and interest income. The tax liability on the income earned will be paid

choices.label: C
choices.text: By the trust on the interest income only, and by the individual taxpayer for the dividend income.

choices.label: D
choices.text: By the trust on the dividend income only, and by the individual taxpayer for the interest income.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §677(a), the grantor is treated as the owner of any portion of a trust whose income is, or may be, distributed to the grantor without the consent of an adverse party. Under §671, the income of that portion is taxed directly to the grantor, even if the trust is irrevocable. Because the individual retained the right to all trust income for life, both the dividends and the interest are taxed entirely to the individual.

Making the trust irrevocable does not shift the tax on income the grantor keeps, so the trust does not pay tax on any of this income. Splitting the tax between the trust and the individual according to whether the income is dividends or interest has no basis in the grantor trust rules; the character of the income does not change who is taxed.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §677(a)により、信託所得が委託者に分配される（または分配されうる）部分については、委託者がその所有者として扱われる。§671により、その部分の所得は信託が撤回不能であっても委託者に直接課税される。本問の個人は生涯にわたり信託所得すべてを受け取る権利を留保しているので、配当も利息も全額が個人に課税される。

撤回不能にしても委託者が受け取る所得の課税は移らないため、信託が税を負担することはない。配当か利息かによって信託と個人で課税を分けるという規定はグランター・トラストのルールにはなく、所得の種類は納税者を変えない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.19 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Which of the following types of business may not qualify for a 501(c)(3) exemption from federal income taxes?
questions.explanation:
IRC §501(c)(3) exempts "corporations, and any community chest, fund, or foundation" organized and operated exclusively for religious, charitable, scientific, educational, or similar purposes. A partnership is not among the listed forms of organization, so a partnership may not qualify for 501(c)(3) exemption.

A foundation, a fund, and a corporation are each expressly listed in §501(c)(3) and can qualify if they meet the organizational and operational tests.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §501(c)(3)は、宗教・慈善・科学・教育などの目的のためにのみ組織・運営される「法人、共同募金、基金（fund）、財団（foundation）」を免税とする。パートナーシップはこの列挙に含まれないため、501(c)(3)の免税資格を得られない。

財団、基金、法人はいずれも§501(c)(3)に明記されており、組織要件・運営要件を満たせば免税資格を得られる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.20 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: This year, Beck gave $5,000 cash to a nephew, canceled $3,000 of the same nephew's indebtedness, donated $1,500 to a political party, and gave $1,200 of municipal bonds to a parent. What is the amount of Beck's gifts before considering the gift tax annual exclusion?
questions.explanation:
A gift is any transfer for less than full consideration (IRC §2511). Cash to the nephew, forgiveness of the nephew's debt (Treas. Reg. §25.2511-1(a)), and municipal bonds given to a parent are all gifts at their fair market value. Under §2501(a)(4), transfers to a political organization for its use are not subject to gift tax.

Gifts = $5,000 + $3,000 + $1,200 = $9,200

The $10,700 amount includes the $1,500 political contribution. The $8,000 amount omits the municipal bonds, and the $5,000 amount counts only the cash gift; canceling the nephew's debt and transferring bonds are also gifts.
questions.explanationJa:
贈与とは、十分な対価を受けない財産の移転をいう（IRC §2511）。甥への現金、甥の債務の免除（Treas. Reg. §25.2511-1(a)）、親への地方債の譲渡は、いずれも時価で贈与となる。政治団体への拠出は§2501(a)(4)により贈与税の対象外である。

贈与額 = $5,000 + $3,000 + $1,200 = $9,200

$10,700は政治献金$1,500を含めた額。$8,000は地方債を漏らした額、$5,000は現金だけの額で、債務免除と債券の譲渡も贈与に当たる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.29 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Which of the following items is not normally taken into account in determining distributable net income of a simple trust?
questions.explanation:
Distributable net income (DNI) is the trust's taxable income with specified modifications under IRC §643(a). One modification is that no deduction is taken for the personal exemption allowed to trusts under §642(b) (§643(a)(2)). Therefore the personal exemption is not taken into account in determining DNI.

Tax-exempt interest is added back in computing DNI under §643(a)(5), net of allocable expenses. Fiduciary fees are deductible expenses that reduce DNI, and taxable interest income is included in DNI.
questions.explanationJa:
分配可能純所得（DNI）は、信託の課税所得にIRC §643(a)の調整を加えて計算する。その調整の一つとして、§642(b)で信託に認められる人的控除は差し引かない（§643(a)(2)）。したがって人的控除はDNIの計算に含めない。

非課税利息は、配賦される費用を差し引いた純額でDNIに加算される（§643(a)(5)）。受託者報酬はDNIを減らす控除項目であり、課税される利息収入はDNIに含まれる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.39 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: A simple trust had $25,000 in capital gains, $10,000 in municipal interest, $5,000 in corporate bond interest, and $2,000 in accounting and trustee fees. According to the trust agreement, capital gains are to be distributed to the beneficiary. What is the distributable net income for this trust?
questions.explanation:
DNI starts with the trust's income and makes the modifications in IRC §643(a). Capital gains are normally excluded from DNI because they are allocated to corpus (§643(a)(3)), but they are included when the governing instrument requires them to be distributed to the beneficiary (Treas. Reg. §1.643(a)-3(b)). Tax-exempt municipal interest is included in DNI (§643(a)(5)), and the accounting and trustee fees are deducted.

Capital gains required to be distributed = $25,000
Municipal interest = $10,000
Corporate bond interest = $5,000
Less accounting and trustee fees = ($2,000)
DNI = $38,000

The $40,000 amount omits the $2,000 of fees. The $28,000 amount excludes the municipal interest, which is part of DNI. The $30,000 amount excludes the municipal interest and does not deduct the fees.
questions.explanationJa:
DNIは信託の所得にIRC §643(a)の調整を加えて計算する。キャピタルゲインは元本に配分されるので通常はDNIから除外されるが（§643(a)(3)）、信託証書で受益者への分配が求められている場合はDNIに含まれる（Treas. Reg. §1.643(a)-3(b)）。非課税の地方債利息もDNIに含まれ（§643(a)(5)）、会計・受託者報酬は差し引く。

分配が求められるキャピタルゲイン = $25,000
地方債利息 = $10,000
社債利息 = $5,000
会計・受託者報酬 = ($2,000)
DNI = $38,000

$40,000は報酬$2,000を差し引いていない額。$28,000はDNIに含まれる地方債利息を除外した額。$30,000は地方債利息を除外し、報酬も差し引いていない額である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.40 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: A taxpayer died in year 1 with a gross estate valued at $100,000,000. In the taxpayer's will, he gave $40,000,000 of his gross estate to his surviving spouse, with no restrictions. His surviving spouse also receives $20,000,000 in assets not included in the taxpayer's gross estate. What is the amount of the marital deduction for the taxpayer's estate?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §2056(a), the estate tax marital deduction equals the value of property that is included in the decedent's gross estate and passes from the decedent to the surviving spouse (and is not a nondeductible terminable interest). The decedent left $40,000,000 of the gross estate to the spouse with no restrictions, so the marital deduction is $40,000,000.

The $20,000,000 of assets the spouse receives outside the gross estate did not pass from the decedent through the estate, so it is not included in the deduction; the $60,000,000 amount wrongly adds it, and the $20,000,000 amount counts only those excluded assets. The $0 amount ignores that an unrestricted bequest to a surviving spouse qualifies for the deduction.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §2056(a)により、遺産税の配偶者控除は、被相続人の総遺産に含まれ、被相続人から生存配偶者に移転する財産（控除不可の終了権益を除く）の価額である。被相続人は総遺産のうち$40,000,000を無条件で配偶者に遺したので、配偶者控除は$40,000,000となる。

配偶者が総遺産以外で受け取る$20,000,000は遺産を通じて被相続人から移転したものではないので控除に含まれない。$60,000,000はそれを加えた誤り、$20,000,000はその対象外の資産だけを数えた額である。$0は配偶者への無条件の遺贈が控除の対象になることを無視している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.8 (AICPA No. 65537)

questions.stem: An executor paid the following on behalf of an estate: $3,500 for attorney's fees, $1,000 for a burial lot, $5,000 of state estate tax, and a $750 credit card debt of the decedent. What amount can be deducted from the gross estate?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §2053(a), the gross estate is reduced by funeral expenses, administration expenses and claims against the estate (debts of the decedent). Under IRC §2058, state estate taxes paid are also deductible in computing the taxable estate. All four payments are therefore deductible.

Attorney's fees (administration expense) = $3,500
Burial lot (funeral expense) = $1,000
State estate tax (§2058) = $5,000
Credit card debt (claim against the estate) = $750
Total deduction = $10,250

The $3,500 amount includes only the attorney's fees. The $4,250 amount adds only the credit card debt to the attorney's fees, omitting the burial lot and the state estate tax. The $5,250 amount omits the $5,000 state estate tax, which is deductible under §2058.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §2053(a) により、葬儀費用、遺産管理費用、遺産に対する債権（被相続人の債務）は総遺産額から控除できる。さらに IRC §2058 により、州の遺産税も課税遺産額の計算上控除できる。したがって4つの支払はすべて控除対象となる。

弁護士報酬（管理費用）$3,500 + 墓地（葬儀費用）$1,000 + 州遺産税 $5,000 + クレジットカード債務 $750 = $10,250

$3,500 は弁護士報酬のみ。$4,250 は弁護士報酬とクレジットカード債務だけで、墓地と州遺産税を漏らしている。$5,250 は §2058 で控除できる州遺産税 $5,000 を漏らしている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.24 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Each of the following may qualify as a tax-exempt organization, except

choices.label: A
choices.text: A community savings and loan association.

questions.explanation:
IRC §501(c) lists the types of organizations that may be exempt from federal income tax. A community savings and loan association is a for-profit financial institution and does not qualify as such an organization; only credit unions without capital stock and certain mutual reserve-fund organizations qualify under §501(c)(14).

A country club may qualify as a social club under §501(c)(7). An amateur sports association may qualify under §501(c)(3) (fostering national or international amateur sports competition). A domestic fraternal society may qualify under §501(c)(8) or §501(c)(10).
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §501(c) は連邦所得税が免除されうる団体の種類を列挙している。地域の貯蓄貸付組合（savings and loan association）は営利の金融機関であり、この列挙に該当しない。§501(c)(14) で免税となるのは資本金を持たない信用組合など一部の相互組織に限られる。

カントリークラブは社交クラブとして §501(c)(7) で、アマチュアスポーツ団体は §501(c)(3)（アマチュアスポーツ競技の振興）で、国内の友愛団体は §501(c)(8) または §501(c)(10) で免税となりうる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.32 (AICPA No. 76128)

questions.stem: A taxpayer died, leaving a large estate. At that time, the taxpayer solely owned a $1,000,000 life insurance policy listing the surviving spouse and each of three children as equal beneficiaries. What is the estate tax marital deduction, if any, for this policy?
questions.explanation:
Life insurance proceeds on a policy the decedent owned are included in the gross estate (IRC §2042). The estate tax marital deduction is allowed only for the value of property included in the gross estate that passes to the surviving spouse (IRC §2056(a)). The spouse is one of four equal beneficiaries.

Gross estate inclusion = $1,000,000
Amount passing to the surviving spouse = $1,000,000 / 4 = $250,000
Marital deduction = $250,000

The $0 amount ignores that the spouse's share passes to the spouse and qualifies. The $500,000 amount gives the spouse half of the proceeds rather than one-fourth. The $1,000,000 amount treats the entire policy as passing to the spouse, but three-fourths passes to the children and does not qualify.
questions.explanationJa:
被相続人が所有していた生命保険契約の保険金は総遺産額に含まれる（IRC §2042）。遺産税の配偶者控除は、総遺産額に含まれる財産のうち生存配偶者に移転する部分についてのみ認められる（IRC §2056(a)）。本問では配偶者は4人の均等な受取人の1人である。

総遺産額への算入 = $1,000,000
配偶者が受け取る額 = $1,000,000 ÷ 4 = $250,000
配偶者控除 = $250,000

$0 は配偶者の受取分が控除対象となることを無視している。$500,000 は配偶者の取り分を4分の1ではなく半分としている。$1,000,000 は全額が配偶者に移転するとしているが、4分の3は子どもに移転するので控除対象とならない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.10 (AICPA No. 72289)

questions.stem: A $50,000 cash gift will reduce an individual's unified credit against gift tax if the gift is made to a

choices.label: C
choices.text: Spouse who is a U.S. citizen.

questions.explanation:
The unified credit is used only when a gift is a taxable gift. A $50,000 cash gift to a 14-year-old child is a present-interest gift that qualifies for the inflation-indexed annual exclusion (IRC §2503(b)), but $50,000 exceeds that exclusion, and no deduction applies to a gift to a child. The excess is a taxable gift that uses part of the donor's unified credit.

Gifts to a U.S. university and to a U.S. church are fully deductible as charitable gifts (IRC §2522), and a gift to a spouse who is a U.S. citizen is fully deductible under the unlimited gift tax marital deduction (IRC §2523). None of these produces a taxable gift, so they do not reduce the unified credit.
questions.explanationJa:
統一税額控除（unified credit）が使われるのは課税贈与がある場合だけである。14歳の子への現金 $50,000 の贈与は現在利益の贈与として、インフレ調整される年間非課税枠（IRC §2503(b)）の対象となるが、$50,000 はその枠を超え、子への贈与には控除もない。超過分は課税贈与となり、贈与者の統一税額控除を使う。

米国の大学や教会への贈与は慈善贈与として全額控除され（IRC §2522）、米国市民である配偶者への贈与は無制限の配偶者控除で全額控除される（IRC §2523）。いずれも課税贈与が生じないので、統一税額控除は減らない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.31 (AICPA No. 70991)

questions.stem:
Lake Trust, a simple trust, reported the following items of income and expense during the year:

Dividend income | $2,500
Taxable interest income | 2,000
Capital gains (allocable to corpus) | 5,000
Accounting fees (allocable to income) | (500)
Trustee fees (allocable to income) | (750)

What is Lake's distributable net income?
questions.explanation:
Distributable net income (DNI) is the trust's taxable income with certain modifications (IRC §643(a)). Capital gains allocated to corpus and not paid, credited or required to be distributed to beneficiaries are excluded from DNI (IRC §643(a)(3)). Deductible expenses such as accounting and trustee fees reduce DNI.

Dividend income = $2,500
Taxable interest income = $2,000
Less accounting fees = ($500)
Less trustee fees = ($750)
DNI = $3,250

The $9,500 amount includes the $5,000 capital gain allocated to corpus and ignores the fees. The $8,250 amount deducts the fees but still includes the capital gain. The $5,000 amount is the capital gain alone, which is excluded from DNI.
questions.explanationJa:
distributable net income（DNI）は、信託の課税所得に一定の修正を加えたものである（IRC §643(a)）。元本（corpus）に配分され、受益者に分配・計上・分配義務のないキャピタルゲインは DNI から除外する（IRC §643(a)(3)）。会計報酬や受託者報酬などの控除可能な費用は DNI を減らす。

配当 $2,500 + 課税利息 $2,000 − 会計報酬 $500 − 受託者報酬 $750 = DNI $3,250

$9,500 は元本に配分されたキャピタルゲイン $5,000 を含め、費用も差し引いていない。$8,250 は費用を差し引いているがキャピタルゲインを含めている。$5,000 は DNI から除外されるキャピタルゲインそのものである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part1 Q.25 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Which of the following payments requires the filing of a gift tax return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $20,000 tuition payment to XYZ College for a friend.

choices.label: B
choices.text: $20,000 medical payment to a doctor for a friend.

questions.explanation:
A gift tax return (Form 709) must be filed by an individual who makes gifts to any one donee during the year that exceed the annual exclusion, other than gifts that are excluded in full (IRC §6019). The annual exclusion is an inflation-indexed amount that is below $20,000 ($19,000 for 2025), so a $20,000 cash gift to a friend exceeds it and requires a gift tax return, even though no gift tax may be due because of the unified credit.

A tuition payment made directly to an educational organization and a medical payment made directly to the provider of medical care are qualified transfers that are excluded from gifts in unlimited amounts (IRC §2503(e)), so they do not require a return. A transfer to a political organization is not subject to gift tax (IRC §2501(a)(4)) and does not require a return.
questions.explanationJa:
1年間に同一の受贈者に対して年間非課税枠を超える贈与をした個人は、全額が除外される贈与を除き、贈与税申告書（Form 709）を提出しなければならない（IRC §6019）。年間非課税枠はインフレ調整される$20,000未満の額（2025年は$19,000）なので、友人への現金$20,000の贈与は枠を超え、統一税額控除により納税額が生じなくても申告が必要である。

教育機関に直接支払う授業料と、医療提供者に直接支払う医療費は、金額の制限なく贈与から除外される（§2503(e)）ため申告は不要。政治団体への移転も贈与税の対象外（§2501(a)(4)）で申告は不要。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.10 (AICPA No. 60783)

questions.stem: Which of the following types of organizations is considered a public charity for purposes of the charitable contribution deduction?
questions.explanation:
Public charities are the organizations described in IRC §170(b)(1), to which an individual may contribute up to the 50% (60% for cash) AGI limitation. Churches and conventions or associations of churches are listed in §170(b)(1), so religious organizations are public charities.

Chambers of commerce are business leagues exempt under §501(c)(6); contributions to them are not deductible as charitable contributions. Supplemental unemployment benefit trusts are exempt under §501(c)(17) and are not charitable organizations. Cemetery companies may receive deductible contributions under §170(c)(5), but they are not public charities; contributions to them are subject to the 30% limitation for non-50% organizations.
questions.explanationJa:
パブリック・チャリティは IRC §170(b)(1) に列挙された団体で、個人はAGIの50%（現金は60%）を限度に寄附金控除できる。教会およびその連合体は §170(b)(1) に列挙されており、宗教団体はパブリック・チャリティに当たる。

商工会議所は §501(c)(6) の事業者団体で、寄附金控除の対象外。補足的失業給付信託は §501(c)(17) の免税団体で、慈善団体ではない。墓地会社への寄附は §170(c)(5) により控除できるが、パブリック・チャリティではなく30%限度の団体に当たる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.21 (AICPA No. 66359)

questions.stem: Which of the following is a requirement for a simple trust?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The trust must not have a charitable beneficiary.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The trust must distribute its entire corpus currently.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The trust must adopt the cash method of accounting.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The trust must make no distribution of its income currently.

questions.explanation:
A simple trust is a trust whose governing instrument requires that all of its income be distributed currently, that does not provide for any amounts to be paid, permanently set aside, or used for charitable purposes, and that does not distribute corpus during the year (IRC §651(a); Treas. Reg. §1.651(a)-1). A simple trust therefore must not have a charitable beneficiary; a trust that can make charitable contributions is a complex trust.

A simple trust must distribute its income currently, not its entire corpus; a trust that distributes corpus in a year is treated as a complex trust for that year. There is no requirement that a simple trust adopt the cash method of accounting. A trust that makes no current distribution of income is the opposite of a simple trust, which is required to distribute all of its income currently.
questions.explanationJa:
単純信託（simple trust）とは、信託証書により全所得を当期に分配することが求められ、慈善目的への支払・積立・使用の定めがなく、その年に元本を分配しない信託をいう（IRC §651(a)、Treas. Reg. §1.651(a)-1）。したがって単純信託は慈善の受益者を持てない。慈善寄附ができる信託は複合信託（complex trust）である。

単純信託が当期に分配しなければならないのは所得であって元本全部ではなく、元本を分配した年は複合信託として扱われる。現金主義を採用しなければならないという要件はない。当期に所得を分配しない信託は、全所得の当期分配を求められる単純信託とは逆である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.42 (AICPA No. 83834)

questions.stem: In determining the amount of taxable gifts, the Internal Revenue Code allows each of the following, except the
questions.explanation:
Taxable gifts are total gifts for the year less the annual exclusion for each donee (IRC §2503(b)), the charitable deduction for gifts to qualified charities (IRC §2522), and the marital deduction for gifts to a spouse (IRC §2523). There is no standard deduction in computing taxable gifts; the standard deduction (IRC §63(c)) is an income tax concept used in computing an individual's taxable income.

The charitable contribution deduction, the gift tax annual exclusion, and the marital deduction are each allowed in determining the amount of taxable gifts.
questions.explanationJa:
課税贈与額は、その年の贈与総額から、受贈者ごとの年間非課税枠（IRC §2503(b)）、適格な慈善団体への贈与に係る寄附金控除（§2522）、配偶者への贈与に係る配偶者控除（§2523）を差し引いて計算する。課税贈与額の計算に標準控除はない。標準控除（§63(c)）は個人の所得税で課税所得を計算するための制度である。

寄附金控除、贈与税の年間非課税枠、配偶者控除は、いずれも課税贈与額の計算で認められる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2021 Recently Released Q.9 (AICPA No. 71105)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about the taxation of trusts?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The basis of property donated to a trust is fair market value at date of gift.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Distributed income is subject to double taxation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The income that is passed through to a beneficiary has the same tax attributes in the hands of the beneficiary as when it is received by the trust.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The trust's income is taxed at a flat rate

questions.explanation:
A trust is a conduit for income it distributes: amounts included in a beneficiary's income have the same character in the beneficiary's hands as in the hands of the trust (IRC §§652(b), 662(b)). For example, tax-exempt interest, qualified dividends, and capital gains included in distributable net income keep that character when passed through to the beneficiary.

Property donated to a trust takes the donor's carryover basis under the gift basis rules (IRC §1015), not fair market value at the date of gift. Distributed income is not subject to double taxation, because the trust deducts the income distribution and the beneficiary reports it, so the income is taxed only once. A trust's retained income is taxed at graduated rates under a compressed rate schedule (IRC §1(e)), not at a flat rate.
questions.explanationJa:
信託は分配する所得の導管であり、受益者の所得に算入される金額は、信託の段階と同じ性質を受益者の手元でも保つ（IRC §652(b), §662(b)）。たとえば分配可能純所得（DNI）に含まれる非課税利子、適格配当、キャピタルゲインは、その性質のまま受益者に引き継がれる。

信託に贈与された資産は贈与の規定（§1015）により贈与者の取得価額を引き継ぎ、贈与時の時価にはならない。分配された所得は信託が分配控除を受け受益者が申告するので1回しか課税されず、二重課税にはならない。信託が留保した所得には累進税率（幅の狭い税率表。§1(e)）が適用され、単一税率ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2021 Recently Released Q.38 (AICPA No. 64307)

questions.stem: If the executor of a decedent's estate elects the alternate valuation date and none of the property included in the gross estate has been sold or distributed, the estate assets must be valued as of how many months after the decedent's death?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §2032, the executor may elect to value the gross estate as of the alternate valuation date, which is six months after the decedent's death. Property sold, distributed, or otherwise disposed of within the six-month period is valued as of the date of disposition; because none of the property was sold or distributed here, all assets are valued six months after death. The election is available only if it reduces both the value of the gross estate and the estate tax (plus GST tax) liability (§2032(c)).
The 12-month figure has no role in the alternate valuation rules. Nine months is the original due date of the estate tax return (Form 706), not the valuation date. Three months is not a period used for alternate valuation.
questions.explanationJa:
遺言執行者は代替評価日を選択でき、その日は死亡日から6か月後です（IRC §2032）。6か月以内に売却・分配された財産はその処分日で評価しますが、本問では売却・分配が無いので、すべての財産を死亡6か月後の時価で評価します。この選択は総遺産額と遺産税額（世代飛越税を含む）の両方が減る場合に限り認められます（§2032(c)）。
12か月は代替評価とは関係のない期間です。9か月は遺産税申告書（Form 706）の当初の提出期限で、評価日ではありません。3か月も代替評価には使われません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.33

questions.stem:
Following are the fair market values of Walters' assets at the date of death. The land was bought by Walters with Walters' funds five years prior to death and held with Walters' sister as joint tenants with right of survivorship.

Asset | Fair market value
Personal effects and jewelry | $100,000
Land held in joint tenancy with sister | $700,000

The executor of Walters' estate did not elect the alternate valuation date. The amount includible as Walters' gross estate in the federal estate tax return is
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §2040(a), property held as joint tenants with right of survivorship by persons other than spouses is included in the decedent's gross estate in full, except to the extent the surviving joint tenant can show that he or she furnished part of the consideration. Walters bought the land entirely with Walters' own funds, so the full $700,000 is included. The personal effects and jewelry are included under §2033.
Gross estate = $100,000 personal effects and jewelry + $700,000 land = $800,000
The $100,000 amount omits the jointly held land, which passes outside probate but is still included under §2040. The $450,000 amount includes only half of the land; the automatic 50% rule of §2040(b) applies only to qualified joint interests between spouses, not to a joint tenancy with a sister. The $700,000 amount omits the personal effects and jewelry.
questions.explanationJa:
配偶者以外との生存者権付き合有財産は、生存した合有者が対価を負担したことを立証できる部分を除き、全額が被相続人の総遺産に含まれます（IRC §2040(a)）。土地は全額 Walters の資金で購入されたので、$700,000 全額を含めます。身の回り品・宝飾品は§2033により含まれます。
総遺産 = 身の回り品・宝飾品 $100,000 + 土地 $700,000 = $800,000
$100,000 は合有の土地を外していますが、検認を経ずに移転する財産でも§2040で総遺産に入ります。$450,000 は土地の半分だけを入れた額で、50%だけ含める§2040(b)は配偶者間の合有に限られ、姉妹との合有には適用されません。$700,000 は身の回り品・宝飾品を外しています。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.34

questions.stem: Income in respect of a cash basis decedent

choices.label: A
choices.text: Covers income earned before the taxpayer's death but not collected until after death

choices.label: B
choices.text: Receives a stepped-up basis in the decedent's estate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Must be included in the decedent's final income tax return

questions.explanation:
Income in respect of a decedent (IRD) under IRC §691 is income the decedent had earned or had a right to receive before death but that was not includible on the decedent's final return under the decedent's (cash) method of accounting. It is taxed to the estate or beneficiary who receives it, when it is received, and it keeps the same character it would have had in the decedent's hands.
The statement that IRD receives a stepped-up basis is incorrect: §1014(c) denies a basis step-up for IRD, which is why its full amount is taxed when collected. The statement that it must be included on the decedent's final return is incorrect because, for a cash basis decedent, uncollected income is by definition not reported on the final return. The statement that it cannot receive capital gain treatment is incorrect because IRD retains its character, so an item such as the unpaid balance of an installment sale of a capital asset produces capital gain to the recipient.
questions.explanationJa:
死亡後に受領する被相続人の所得（IRD、IRC §691）とは、被相続人が生前に稼得し受け取る権利があったが、現金主義のため最終申告書に含まれなかった所得です。実際に受け取った遺産または受益者が、受け取った時に課税され、所得の性質は被相続人の手にあった場合と同じです。
IRD は§1014(c)により取得価額のステップアップを受けないため、「ステップアップを受ける」は誤りです。現金主義の被相続人が未回収の所得は最終申告書に含まれないので、「最終申告書に含める」も誤りです。IRD は性質を引き継ぐため、資本資産の割賦販売の未回収分のようにキャピタルゲインとなるものもあり、「キャピタルゲインにならない」も誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.35

questions.stem: Rose, a calendar-year, cash-basis taxpayer who died in June was entitled to receive a $10,000 fee that had not been collected before the date of death. The executor of Rose's estate collected the full $10,000 in July. This $10,000 should appear in

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only the decedent's final individual income tax return

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only the estate's fiduciary income tax return

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both the fiduciary income tax return and the estate tax return

questions.explanation:
The $10,000 fee is income in respect of a decedent under IRC §691: Rose earned it before death, but as a cash basis taxpayer she had not received it, so it is not reported on her final Form 1040. When the executor collects it, it is gross income of the estate and is reported on the estate's fiduciary income tax return (Form 1041). In addition, the right to receive the fee was property Rose owned at death, so its value is included in her gross estate under §2033 and appears on the estate tax return (Form 706). The double exposure is relieved by the §691(c) deduction for the estate tax attributable to the IRD.
Reporting the fee only on the final individual return is incorrect because a cash basis taxpayer reports income when received, and Rose never received it. Reporting it only on the fiduciary return ignores that the uncollected fee is an asset of the gross estate. Reporting it only on the estate tax return ignores that IRD is taxable income to the estate when collected.
questions.explanationJa:
$10,000 の報酬は IRC §691 の IRD です。Rose は生前に稼得していましたが、現金主義で未受領だったため最終の Form 1040 には含めません。遺言執行者が回収した時点で遺産の総所得となり、遺産の受託者所得税申告書（Form 1041）に記載します。さらに、報酬を受け取る権利は死亡時に Rose が所有していた財産なので、§2033により総遺産に含まれ、遺産税申告書（Form 706）にも載ります。二重課税は、IRD に係る遺産税を所得から控除する§691(c)で調整されます。
最終の個人申告書だけとするのは、現金主義では受領時に所得計上するのに Rose は受け取っていないので誤りです。受託者申告書だけとするのは、未回収の報酬が総遺産の財産であることを見落としています。遺産税申告書だけとするのは、IRD が回収時に遺産の課税所得となることを見落としています。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.36

questions.stem:
Which of the following credits may be offset against the gross estate tax to determine the net estate tax of a U.S. citizen? (The second column is the credit for gift taxes paid on gifts made after 1976.)

Unified credit | Gift tax credit (post-1976 gifts)
questions.explanation:
The unified credit (applicable credit amount) under IRC §2010 is subtracted from the tentative estate tax to determine the net estate tax, so it is allowed.
Gift taxes paid on gifts made after 1976 are not allowed as a credit. Instead, under §2001(b), post-1976 adjusted taxable gifts are added to the taxable estate to compute the tentative tax, and the gift tax payable on those gifts is then subtracted in computing the estate tax itself. Because this subtraction is built into the unified computation, there is no separate credit; the §2012 credit for gift tax applies only to gifts made before 1977.
The combinations that answer Yes for the post-1976 gift tax credit treat the §2001(b)(2) subtraction as a credit, which it is not. The combination answering No for the unified credit is incorrect because §2010 expressly allows that credit against the estate tax.
questions.explanationJa:
統一税額控除（適用控除額、IRC §2010）は、遺産税の暫定税額から差し引いて納付すべき遺産税を求めるので、認められます。
1976年より後の贈与について支払った贈与税は、税額控除としては認められません。§2001(b) では、1976年後の調整課税贈与額を課税遺産額に加算して暫定税額を計算し、その贈与について支払うべき贈与税を税額計算の中で差し引きます。この減算は統一税額計算に組み込まれているため別個の税額控除はなく、§2012の贈与税額控除は1977年前の贈与に限られます。
1976年後の贈与税控除を Yes とする組み合わせは、§2001(b)(2) の減算を税額控除と取り違えています。統一税額控除を No とする組み合わせは、§2010が遺産税からの控除を明文で認めているので誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.37

questions.stem:
Under the provisions of a decedent's will, the following cash disbursements were made by the estate's executor:
I. A charitable bequest to the American Red Cross
II. Payment of the decedent's funeral expenses
What deduction(s) is(are) allowable in determining the decedent's taxable estate?
questions.explanation:
Both disbursements are deductible from the gross estate in arriving at the taxable estate. A bequest to a qualified charity such as the American Red Cross is deductible without limit under IRC §2055. Funeral expenses are deductible under §2053(a)(1), along with administration expenses, claims against the estate, and unpaid mortgages.
Selecting only the charitable bequest omits the §2053 deduction for funeral expenses. Selecting only the funeral expenses omits the unlimited §2055 charitable deduction. Selecting neither ignores both statutory deductions.
questions.explanationJa:
どちらも総遺産から控除して課税遺産額を求めます。American Red Cross のような適格慈善団体への遺贈は IRC §2055により上限なく控除できます。葬儀費用は、管理費用・遺産に対する債務・未払抵当債務と同じく§2053(a)(1)で控除できます。
慈善遺贈だけとすると§2053の葬儀費用控除が漏れ、葬儀費用だけとすると上限の無い§2055の慈善控除が漏れます。どちらも控除できないとするのは両方の規定を無視しています。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.38

questions.stem: Within how many months after the date of a decedent's death is the federal estate tax return (Form 706) due if no extension of time for filing is granted?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §6075(a), the estate tax return (Form 706) is due nine months after the date of the decedent's death. An automatic six-month extension of time to file is available by filing Form 4768 (Treas. Reg. §20.6081-1).
Six months is the length of the extension (and of the alternate valuation period under §2032), not the original due date. The 4½-month and 3½-month periods are not filing deadlines for Form 706.
questions.explanationJa:
遺産税申告書（Form 706）の提出期限は死亡日から9か月後です（IRC §6075(a)）。Form 4768 を提出すれば6か月の自動延長が受けられます（Treas. Reg. §20.6081-1）。
6か月は延長期間（および§2032の代替評価日までの期間）であって当初の期限ではありません。4½か月や3½か月は Form 706 の期限とは関係ありません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.39

questions.stem: Abby and Tom Kehls, both U.S. citizens, are married. All of their real and personal property is owned by them as tenants by the entirety or as joint tenants with right of survivorship. The gross estate of the first spouse to die

choices.label: A
choices.text: Includes 50% of the value of all property owned by the couple, regardless of which spouse furnished the original consideration

choices.label: B
choices.text: Includes only the property that had been acquired with the funds of the deceased spouse

choices.label: C
choices.text: Is governed by the federal statutory provisions relating to jointly held property, rather than by the decedent's interest in community property vested by state law, if the Kehls reside in a community property state

choices.label: D
choices.text: Includes one-third of the value of all real estate owned by the Kehls, as the dower right in the case of the wife or curtesy right in the case of the husband

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §2040(b), a qualified joint interest, meaning property held by spouses as tenants by the entirety or as joint tenants with right of survivorship where the spouses are the only joint tenants, is treated as owned one-half by each spouse. The gross estate of the first spouse to die therefore includes 50% of the value of the property, regardless of which spouse furnished the consideration.
Including only the property bought with the deceased spouse's funds describes the consideration-furnished test of §2040(a), which applies to joint tenancies with persons other than a spouse. The statement that federal joint-property rules override the decedent's state-law community property interest is incorrect: community property is included under §2033 according to the one-half interest vested in the decedent by state law. There is no one-third dower or curtesy rule for spousal joint property; §2040(b) fixes the inclusion at one-half.
questions.explanationJa:
配偶者だけが合有者である夫婦全体保有（tenancy by the entirety）または生存者権付き合有の財産は「適格合有持分」とされ、各配偶者が2分の1ずつ所有するものとして扱われます（IRC §2040(b)）。したがって先に死亡した配偶者の総遺産には、どちらが購入資金を出したかにかかわらず財産の50%が含まれます。
「死亡した配偶者の資金で取得した財産だけ」は、配偶者以外との合有に適用される§2040(a)の対価負担基準です。共有財産制の州では、被相続人の持分は州法上帰属する2分の1として§2033で含まれるので、連邦の合有財産の規定が優先するという記述は誤りです。配偶者間の合有財産について dower・curtesy による3分の1の規定はなく、§2040(b)で2分の1と決まっています。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.40

questions.stem: Proceeds of a life insurance policy payable to the estate's executor, as the estate's representative, are

choices.label: A
choices.text: Includible in the decedent's gross estate only if the premiums had been paid by the insured

choices.label: B
choices.text: Includible in the decedent's gross estate only if the policy was taken out within three years of the insured's death under the "contemplation of death" rule

choices.label: C
choices.text: Never includible in the decedent's gross estate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Always includible in the decedent's gross estate

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §2042(1), the gross estate includes the proceeds of insurance on the decedent's life receivable by the executor, that is, payable to or for the benefit of the estate. Inclusion does not depend on who owned the policy, who paid the premiums, or when the policy was purchased, so such proceeds are always includible.
The premium-payment condition is not part of §2042(1); premium payment by the insured is not a test for inclusion of proceeds payable to the estate. The three-year rule of §2035 applies to a transfer of a life insurance policy (or incidents of ownership) within three years of death, not to the date a policy was taken out, and it is irrelevant when the proceeds are payable to the executor. Proceeds payable to the executor cannot be never includible, because §2042(1) expressly includes them.
questions.explanationJa:
被相続人を被保険者とする生命保険金のうち、遺言執行者が受け取るもの（遺産に支払われるもの）は総遺産に含まれます（IRC §2042(1)）。保険契約の所有者、保険料の負担者、加入時期にかかわらず含まれるので、常に総遺産に入ります。
保険料を被保険者が負担した場合に限るという条件は§2042(1)にはありません。§2035の3年ルールは死亡前3年以内に保険契約（所有権の諸権利）を移転した場合の規定で、加入時期の規定ではなく、遺言執行者に支払われる保険金には関係しません。§2042(1)が明文で含めているため、「決して含まれない」も誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.41

questions.stem:
Which of the following is (are) deductible from a decedent's gross estate?
I. Expenses of administering and settling the estate
II. State inheritance or estate tax
questions.explanation:
Expenses of administering and settling the estate (executor's commissions, attorney's fees, court costs) are deductible under IRC §2053(a)(2). Estate, inheritance, legacy, or succession taxes actually paid to any state or the District of Columbia are deductible under §2058, which replaced the former state death tax credit for decedents dying after 2004. Both items are therefore deductible from the gross estate.
Selecting only administration expenses omits the §2058 deduction for state death taxes. Selecting only the state tax omits the §2053 deduction for administration expenses. Selecting neither ignores both statutory deductions. (Administration expenses may alternatively be deducted on the estate's income tax return, but under §642(g) they cannot be deducted on both returns.)
questions.explanationJa:
遺産の管理・清算費用（遺言執行者報酬、弁護士費用、裁判費用など）は IRC §2053(a)(2)で控除できます。州に実際に納付した遺産税・相続税は§2058で控除でき、これは2005年以降に死亡した者について従来の州遺産税額控除に代わった規定です。したがって両方とも総遺産から控除できます。
管理費用だけとすると§2058の州税の控除が漏れ、州税だけとすると§2053の管理費用の控除が漏れます。どちらも控除できないとするのは両方の規定を無視しています。（管理費用は遺産の所得税申告書で控除することもできますが、§642(g)により両方で控除することはできません。）
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.42

questions.stem: A complex trust is a trust that

choices.label: A
choices.text: Is exempt from payment of income tax since the tax is paid by the beneficiaries

choices.label: B
choices.text: Invests only in corporate securities and is prohibited from engaging in short-term transactions

choices.label: C
choices.text: Permits accumulation of current income, provides for charitable contributions, or distributes principal during the taxable year

choices.label: D
choices.text: Must distribute income currently, but is prohibited from distributing principal during the taxable year

questions.explanation:
A simple trust under IRC §651 is one that must distribute all of its income currently, makes no charitable contributions, and does not distribute principal during the year. Any trust that does not meet all of those conditions, because it may accumulate income, provides for charitable contributions, or distributes principal, is a complex trust taxed under §§661-663.
The statement that a complex trust is exempt from income tax is incorrect; a complex trust is a separate taxpayer that pays tax on income it accumulates and deducts only amounts distributed. The statement about investing only in corporate securities describes an investment restriction, which has nothing to do with the simple/complex classification. The statement that the trust must distribute income currently and may not distribute principal describes a simple trust.
questions.explanationJa:
単純信託（IRC §651）は、所得を毎年すべて分配し、慈善寄附を行わず、その年に元本を分配しない信託です。所得の留保を認める、慈善寄附を予定する、元本を分配する、のいずれかに当たる信託は単純信託の要件を満たさず、複合信託として§661〜663で課税されます。
複合信託は独立した納税者で、留保した所得には信託自身が課税され、分配額だけを控除するので、「所得税が免除される」は誤りです。社債などの投資対象の制限は単純・複合の区分と無関係です。「所得を毎年分配し、元本の分配は禁止」は単純信託の説明です。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.43

questions.stem: The standard deduction for a trust or an estate in the fiduciary income tax return is
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §63(c)(6), which covers estates and trusts, the standard deduction is zero for an estate or trust. Instead of a standard deduction, a fiduciary is allowed a personal exemption under §642(b): $600 for an estate, $300 for a trust required to distribute all income currently, and $100 for any other trust.
The $100, $300, and $600 amounts are the §642(b) exemption amounts for a complex trust, a trust required to distribute all income currently, and an estate, respectively; they are exemptions, not a standard deduction.
questions.explanationJa:
遺産と信託の標準控除はゼロです（IRC §63(c)(6)）。標準控除の代わりに§642(b)の人的控除があり、遺産は $600、所得を毎年全額分配すべき信託は $300、その他の信託は $100 です。
$100・$300・$600 はそれぞれ複合信託・全額分配義務のある信託・遺産の§642(b)の人的控除額で、標準控除ではありません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.44

questions.stem:
Which of the following fiduciary entities are required to use the calendar year as their taxable period for income tax purposes?

Estates | Trusts (except those that are tax exempt)
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §644, a trust (other than a tax-exempt trust or a charitable trust described in §4947(a)(1)) must use the calendar year as its taxable year. An estate is not subject to this rule; the executor may choose a calendar year or any fiscal year ending on the last day of a month within 12 months after the date of death.
The combinations answering Yes for estates are incorrect because §644 applies only to trusts and an estate may adopt a fiscal year. The combination answering No for trusts is incorrect because §644 requires non-exempt trusts to use the calendar year.
questions.explanationJa:
信託（免税信託と§4947(a)(1)の慈善信託を除く）は暦年を課税年度としなければなりません（IRC §644）。遺産にはこの規定が適用されず、遺言執行者は暦年か、死亡後12か月以内のいずれかの月末に終わる事業年度を選べます。
遺産を Yes とする組み合わせは、§644が信託にだけ適用され遺産は事業年度を選べるので誤りです。信託を No とする組み合わせは、§644が免税でない信託に暦年を義務付けているので誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.45

questions.stem: Raff died in Year 1 leaving her entire estate to her only child. Raff's will gave full discretion to the estate's executor with regard to distributions of income. For Year 2, the estate's distributable net income was $15,000, of which $9,000 was paid to the beneficiary. None of the income was tax exempt. What amount can be claimed on the estate's Year 2 fiduciary income tax return for the distributions deduction?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §661(a) and (c), an estate's distribution deduction equals the amounts properly paid, credited, or required to be distributed to beneficiaries, limited to distributable net income (reduced by tax-exempt income included in DNI). Because the executor had discretion, only the amount actually paid counts.
Distribution deduction = lesser of amount distributed $9,000 or DNI $15,000 = $9,000
The $0 amount denies the deduction, but discretionary distributions actually paid qualify under §661(a)(2). The $6,000 amount is the undistributed DNI ($15,000 - $9,000) that remains taxable to the estate. The $15,000 amount is the full DNI, which is only the ceiling; the deduction cannot exceed the $9,000 actually distributed.
questions.explanationJa:
遺産の分配控除は、受益者に実際に支払った（または分配が義務付けられた）額で、分配可能純所得（DNI、免税所得を除く）が上限です（IRC §661(a)(c)）。執行者に裁量があるので、実際に支払った額だけが対象です。
分配控除 = 分配額 $9,000 と DNI $15,000 の小さい方 = $9,000
$0 は控除を認めていませんが、実際に支払った裁量分配は§661(a)(2)で控除できます。$6,000 は分配されなかった DNI（$15,000 - $9,000）で、遺産自身に課税される部分です。$15,000 は DNI 全額で、上限にすぎず、実際の分配額 $9,000 を超えて控除はできません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.46

questions.stem: A distribution from estate income, that was currently required, was made to the estate's sole beneficiary during its calendar year. The maximum amount of the distribution to be included in the beneficiary's gross income is limited to the estate's
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §662(a), a beneficiary includes in gross income the amounts required to be distributed and other amounts properly paid, but the total included cannot exceed the estate's distributable net income (DNI) as defined in §643(a). DNI acts as the ceiling on both the estate's distribution deduction (§661) and the beneficiary's income inclusion.
