Capital gain income is not the limit; capital gains allocated to corpus are generally excluded from DNI. Ordinary gross income is not the limit because DNI is computed after deducting expenses. Net investment income is a concept used for the §1411 surtax and for the investment interest limitation, not for measuring a beneficiary's taxable distribution.
questions.explanationJa:
受益者は、分配が義務付けられた額とその他の分配額を総所得に含めますが、その合計は遺産の分配可能純所得（DNI、§643(a)）が上限です（IRC §662(a)）。DNI は遺産の分配控除（§661）と受益者の所得算入の両方の上限になります。
キャピタルゲインは上限ではなく、元本に配分されたキャピタルゲインは原則として DNI から除かれます。総所得（通常の総収入）は費用控除前の額なので上限ではありません。純投資所得は§1411の追加税や投資利息控除の限度で使う概念で、受益者の課税分配額を測るものではありません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.47

questions.stem:
A distribution to an estate's sole beneficiary for the calendar Year 1 equaled $15,000, the amount currently required to be distributed by the will. The estate's Year 1 records were as follows:

Category | Amount | Description
Estate income | $40,000 | Taxable interest
Estate disbursements | $34,000 | Expenses attributable to taxable interest

What amount of the distribution was taxable to the beneficiary?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §662(a)(1), a beneficiary includes a required distribution in gross income only to the extent of the estate's distributable net income (DNI). DNI under §643(a) is the estate's taxable income before the distribution deduction, here the taxable interest less the expenses attributable to it.
DNI = $40,000 taxable interest - $34,000 expenses = $6,000
Taxable to beneficiary = lesser of distribution $15,000 or DNI $6,000 = $6,000
The $40,000 amount is the estate's gross interest income and ignores both the expenses and the DNI ceiling. The $15,000 amount is the entire distribution; the $9,000 excess over DNI is a nontaxable distribution of corpus. The $0 amount ignores that required distributions carry out DNI to the beneficiary.
questions.explanationJa:
受益者は、分配が義務付けられた額を、遺産の分配可能純所得（DNI）を上限として総所得に含めます（IRC §662(a)(1)）。DNI（§643(a)）は分配控除前の遺産の課税所得で、本問では課税利息からそれに対応する費用を差し引いた額です。
DNI = 課税利息 $40,000 - 費用 $34,000 = $6,000
受益者の課税額 = 分配額 $15,000 と DNI $6,000 の小さい方 = $6,000
$40,000 は遺産の利息収入の総額で、費用も DNI の上限も考慮していません。$15,000 は分配額全額で、DNI を超える $9,000 は課税されない元本の分配です。$0 は、義務的分配によって DNI が受益者へ移ることを無視しています。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.48

questions.stem:
Mill, a cash basis taxpayer, died on January 15, Year 1. In Year 1, the estate executor made the required periodic distribution of $8,000 from estate income to Mill's sole heir. The following pertains to the estate's income and disbursements in Year 1:

Category | Amount | Description
Estate income | $40,000 | Taxable interest
Estate income | $20,000 | Net LT capital gains allocable to corpus
Estate disbursements | $10,000 | Admin expenses allocable to taxable income

For the calendar Year 1, what was the estate's distributable net income (DNI)?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §643(a), distributable net income is the estate's taxable income computed without the distribution deduction and the personal exemption, and excluding capital gains that are allocated to corpus and not paid, credited, or required to be distributed to beneficiaries.
DNI = $40,000 taxable interest - $10,000 administrative expenses = $30,000
The $20,000 of net long-term capital gains is allocated to corpus, so it is excluded under §643(a)(3).
The $40,000 amount omits the deduction for administrative expenses. The $50,000 amount ($40,000 + $20,000 - $10,000) wrongly includes the capital gains allocated to corpus. The $60,000 amount is total gross income, including the corpus capital gains and ignoring the expenses.
questions.explanationJa:
分配可能純所得（DNI）は、分配控除と人的控除を差し引く前の遺産の課税所得から、元本に配分され受益者に分配されないキャピタルゲインを除いた額です（IRC §643(a)）。
DNI = 課税利息 $40,000 - 管理費用 $10,000 = $30,000
長期キャピタルゲイン $20,000 は元本に配分されるので、§643(a)(3)により DNI から除きます。
$40,000 は管理費用を差し引いていません。$50,000（$40,000 + $20,000 - $10,000）は元本に配分されたキャピタルゲインを誤って含めています。$60,000 は元本のキャピタルゲインを含めた総収入で、費用も差し引いていません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.49

questions.stem:
Mill, a cash basis taxpayer, died on January 15, Year 1. In Year 1, the estate executor made the required periodic distribution of $8,000 from estate income to Mill's sole heir. The following pertains to the estate's income and disbursements in Year 1:

Category | Amount | Description
Estate income | $40,000 | Taxable interest
Estate income | $20,000 | Net LT capital gains allocable to corpus
Estate disbursements | $10,000 | Admin expenses allocable to taxable income

Mill's executor does not intend to file an extension request for the estate fiduciary income tax return. By what date must the executor file the Form 1041, U.S. Fiduciary Income Tax Return, for the estate's calendar Year 1?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §6072(a), Form 1041 for a calendar-year estate is due on the 15th day of the fourth month after the close of the taxable year, which is April 15. Under §7503, when the due date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, the return is timely if filed on the next business day; in the year described, that moves the deadline to Monday, April 17, Year 2.
March 15 is the due date for calendar-year partnership (Form 1065) and S corporation (Form 1120-S) returns, not Form 1041. June 15 is not a filing deadline for Form 1041. September 15 is the extended due date for partnership and S corporation returns; an estate that requests the automatic extension for Form 1041 has until September 30, and Mill's executor is not requesting an extension in any case.
questions.explanationJa:
暦年の遺産の Form 1041 の期限は、課税年度終了後4か月目の15日、すなわち4月15日です（IRC §6072(a)）。期限が土曜・日曜・法定休日に当たる場合は翌営業日に提出すれば期限内とされ（§7503）、本問の年はYear 2 の4月17日（月曜日）が期限になります。
3月15日は暦年のパートナーシップ（Form 1065）と S 法人（Form 1120-S）の期限で、Form 1041 の期限ではありません。6月15日は Form 1041 の期限ではありません。9月15日はパートナーシップと S 法人の延長後の期限で、Form 1041 の自動延長後の期限は9月30日です。そもそも本問の執行者は延長を申請しません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.50

questions.stem: Under the unified rate schedule,

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lifetime taxable gifts are taxed on a noncumulative basis.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Transfers at death are taxed on a noncumulative basis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lifetime taxable gifts and transfers at death are taxed on a cumulative basis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The gift tax rates are 5% higher than the estate tax rates.

questions.explanation:
The gift tax and the estate tax share a single unified rate schedule (IRC §2001(c), §2502(a)). Both taxes are computed cumulatively: the gift tax for the current year is computed on all taxable gifts made in the current and prior periods, less the tax on prior-period gifts (§2502(a)), and the estate tax is computed on the taxable estate plus adjusted taxable gifts made after 1976, less gift tax payable on those gifts (§2001(b)). Therefore lifetime taxable gifts and transfers at death are taxed on a cumulative basis.

The statement that lifetime taxable gifts are taxed on a noncumulative basis is wrong because each year's gift tax takes all prior taxable gifts into account. The statement that transfers at death are taxed on a noncumulative basis is wrong because adjusted taxable gifts are added to the taxable estate. The statement that gift tax rates are 5% higher than estate tax rates is wrong because one rate schedule applies to both taxes.
questions.explanationJa:
贈与税と遺産税は統一税率表（IRC §2001(c)、§2502(a)）を共有し、どちらも累積ベースで課税されます。贈与税は当年と過去の課税贈与の合計に税率を当て、過去分の税額を差し引いて計算します。遺産税も課税遺産に1976年後の調整課税贈与を加えて計算し、その贈与に係る贈与税を差し引きます。したがって「生前の課税贈与と死亡時の移転はいずれも累積ベースで課税される」が正しい記述です。

生前贈与を非累積で課税するという記述は、過去の贈与を合算する仕組みと矛盾します。死亡時の移転を非累積で課税するという記述も、調整課税贈与を加算する点と矛盾します。贈与税率が遺産税率より5%高いという記述は、同一の税率表を使うことと矛盾します。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.52

questions.stem: The generation-skipping transfer tax is imposed

choices.label: C
choices.text: As a separate tax in addition to the gift and estate taxes

choices.label: D
choices.text: On transfers of future interest to beneficiaries who are more than one generation above the donor's generation

questions.explanation:
The generation-skipping transfer (GST) tax under IRC §2601 is a separate tax imposed on every generation-skipping transfer (a direct skip, taxable termination, or taxable distribution). It applies in addition to any gift tax or estate tax due on the same transfer, at the maximum estate tax rate times the inclusion ratio (§2641), subject to the GST exemption (§2631).

The GST tax does not replace the gift tax or the estate tax; a direct skip made by gift can owe both gift tax and GST tax, and a direct skip at death can owe both estate tax and GST tax. The description of transfers to beneficiaries more than one generation above the donor is wrong because a skip person is a beneficiary two or more generations below the transferor (§2613), and the tax is not limited to future interests.
questions.explanationJa:
世代跳躍移転税（GST税、IRC §2601）は、直接スキップ・課税終了・課税分配といった世代跳躍移転に課される独立の税で、同じ移転に対する贈与税や遺産税に「上乗せ」して課されます。税率は遺産税の最高税率に包含比率を掛けたもの（§2641）で、GST非課税枠（§2631）があります。

贈与税や遺産税の「代わりに」課されるわけではなく、贈与による直接スキップでは贈与税とGST税の両方が生じ得ます。また、スキップ・パーソンは移転者より2世代以上「下」の受益者であり（§2613）、「上」の世代への将来権の移転という記述は誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.53

questions.stem: During Year 1, Morgan transferred a corporate bond with a face amount and fair market value of $20,000 to a trust for the benefit of her 16-year old child. Annual interest on this bond is $2,000, which is to be accumulated in the trust and distributed to the child on reaching the age of 21. The bond is then to be distributed to the donor or her successor-in-interest in liquidation of the trust. Present value of the total interest to be received by the child is $8,710. The amount of the gift that is excludable from taxable gifts is
questions.explanation:
The annual gift tax exclusion applies only to gifts of present interests (IRC §2503(b); Treas. Reg. §25.2503-3). The only gift here is the child's income interest, worth $8,710 (the bond itself reverts to Morgan or her successor, so it is not a gift). Because the interest must be accumulated and is not paid to the child until age 21, the child has no unrestricted right to the immediate use or enjoyment of the income, so the gift is a future interest.

The §2503(c) exception for gifts to minors does not apply because the trust does not permit the income to be expended for the child before age 21; it requires accumulation. Excludable amount = $0.

The $8,710 amount is the value of the gift, but it is a future interest and is not excludable. The $10,000 amount corresponds to the annual exclusion of earlier years (the exclusion is indexed for inflation and is higher today), but no annual exclusion is available for a future interest in any year. The $20,000 amount is the value of the bond, which is not given to the child because it returns to the donor.
questions.explanationJa:
贈与税の年間非課税枠は「現在権（present interest）」の贈与にしか使えません（IRC §2503(b)、Treas. Reg. §25.2503-3）。本問で子に贈与されたのは利息の受益権（現在価値 $8,710）だけで、債券本体は信託終了時に贈与者側へ戻るため贈与ではありません。利息は信託内で積み立てられ21歳まで子に支払われないので、子は直ちに使用・享受する権利を持たず、将来権の贈与になります。

未成年者向けの §2503(c) の例外も、21歳前に子のために支出できる定めがなく積立が義務付けられているため適用されません。よって非課税となる額は $0 です。

$8,710 は贈与額そのものですが将来権のため除外できません。$10,000 は過去の年度の年間非課税枠の額で（非課税枠は物価調整され現在はより高額です）、どの年度でも将来権には使えません。$20,000 は債券の価額で、贈与者へ戻るため子への贈与ではありません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.54

questions.stem: Which of the following requires filing a gift tax return, if the transfer exceeds the available annual gift tax exclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Medical expenses paid directly to a physician on behalf of an individual unrelated to the donor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tuition paid directly to an accredited university on behalf of an individual unrelated to the donor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Payments for college books, supplies, and dormitory fees on behalf of an individual unrelated to the donor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Campaign expenses paid to a political organization

questions.explanation:
IRC §2503(e) excludes from taxable gifts, without limit and regardless of the relationship to the donor, amounts paid directly to a qualifying educational organization for tuition and amounts paid directly to a provider for medical care. The exclusion covers tuition only; books, supplies, and dormitory (room and board) fees are not qualified transfers. Payments for college books, supplies, and dormitory fees are therefore ordinary gifts, and a gift tax return (Form 709) is required when they exceed the annual exclusion (§6019).

Medical expenses paid directly to a physician and tuition paid directly to an accredited university are qualified transfers under §2503(e), so no return is required for them. Transfers to a political organization for its use are not subject to gift tax under §2501(a)(4), so campaign contributions do not require a return.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §2503(e) により、教育機関へ直接支払う授業料と医療提供者へ直接支払う医療費は、金額の上限なく、受贈者との関係を問わず課税贈与から除外されます。ただし対象は授業料だけで、教科書・用品・寮費は含まれません。そのため大学の教科書・用品・寮費の支払いは通常の贈与となり、年間非課税枠を超えれば贈与税申告書（Form 709）の提出が必要です（§6019）。

医師へ直接支払った医療費と大学へ直接支払った授業料は §2503(e) の適格移転なので申告は不要です。政治団体への移転は §2501(a)(4) により贈与税の対象外で、選挙資金の支払いも申告は不要です。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Partnerships, Estate, Trust Q.56

questions.stem:
Which of the following credits may be offset against the gross estate tax to determine the net estate tax of a U.S. Citizen?
Unified credit | Credit for gift taxes paid on gifts made after 1976
questions.explanation:
The unified (applicable) credit under IRC §2010 is subtracted from the estate tax. Gift taxes on gifts made after 1976 are not a credit. Instead, under §2001(b), adjusted taxable gifts are added to the taxable estate to compute the tentative tax, and the gift tax payable on those post-1976 gifts is then subtracted in arriving at the estate tax. The §2012 credit for gift tax applies only to gifts made before 1977.
Yes | Yes and No | Yes treat post-1976 gift taxes as a credit, which they are not. No | No and No | Yes deny the unified credit, which every U.S. citizen's estate may claim.
questions.explanationJa:
統一税額控除（IRC §2010）は遺産税から差し引けます。一方、1976年より後の贈与に係る贈与税は「税額控除」ではありません。§2001(b) により調整課税贈与を課税遺産に加算して仮の税額を計算し、その贈与について支払うべき贈与税を差し引く仕組みです。贈与税の税額控除（§2012）は1977年より前の贈与だけが対象です。
したがって統一税額控除は Yes、1976年後の贈与税の税額控除は No です。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Property Taxation Q.29

questions.stem:
Under the provisions of a decedent's will, the following cash disbursements were made by the estate's executor:
I. A charitable bequest to the American Red Cross
II. Payment of the decedent's funeral expenses
What deduction(s) is(are) allowable in determining the decedent's taxable estate?
questions.explanation:
The taxable estate equals the gross estate less allowable deductions. IRC §2055 allows an unlimited deduction for bequests to qualified charitable organizations such as the American Red Cross, and IRC §2053(a)(1) allows a deduction for funeral expenses. Both disbursements are therefore deductible.
"I only" overlooks the funeral expense deduction, "II only" overlooks the charitable deduction, and "Neither I nor II" denies both.
questions.explanationJa: 課税遺産額は総遺産額から控除額を差し引いて求めます。適格な慈善団体（米国赤十字など）への遺贈は IRC §2055 により上限なく控除でき、葬儀費用は §2053(a)(1) により控除できます。したがって両方とも控除可能です。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Property Taxation Q.30

questions.stem: Proceeds of a life insurance policy payable to the estate's executor, as the estate's representative, are

choices.label: A
choices.text: Includible in the decedent's gross estate only if the premiums had been paid by the insured

choices.label: B
choices.text: Includible in the decedent's gross estate only if the policy was taken out within three years of the insured's death under the "contemplation of death" rule

choices.label: C
choices.text: Never includable in the decedent's gross estate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Always includable in the decedent's gross estate

questions.explanation:
IRC §2042(1) includes in the gross estate the proceeds of insurance on the decedent's life that are receivable by the executor (as representative of the estate), regardless of who paid the premiums, who owned the policy, or when it was purchased.
The premium-payment test is not a condition for §2042(1) inclusion. The three-year "contemplation of death" rule (§2035) concerns transfers of a policy within three years of death, not proceeds payable to the executor. Proceeds payable to the executor are never excluded.
questions.explanationJa:
被相続人の生命保険金のうち、遺産の代表者としての遺言執行者が受け取るものは、保険料の負担者・契約者・加入時期にかかわらず、IRC §2042(1) によりすべて総遺産に含まれます。
保険料の負担者は §2042(1) の要件ではありません。死亡前3年以内のルール（§2035）は保険契約の移転に関するもので、執行者が受け取る保険金には関係しません。執行者受取りの保険金が除外されることはありません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Property Taxation Q.31

questions.stem:
Following are the fair market values of Wald's assets at the date of death. The land was bought by Wald with Wald's funds five years prior to death and was held with Wald's sister as joint tenants with right of survivorship.

Asset | Fair market value
Personal effects and jewelry | $150,000
Land held in JTWROS with sister | $1,800,000

The executor of Wald's estate did not elect the alternate valuation date. The amount includible as Wald's gross estate in the federal estate tax return is
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §2040(a), property held as joint tenants with right of survivorship by persons other than spouses is included in the decedent's gross estate in full, except to the extent the survivor can show contribution to the purchase price. Wald furnished all of the funds, so the entire $1,800,000 is included. Personal effects are included under §2033.
Gross estate = $150,000 + $1,800,000 = $1,950,000
The $150,000 amount omits the jointly held land. The $1,150,000 amount includes only half of the land, which is the rule for spouses' qualified joint interests under §2040(b), not for a sister. The $1,800,000 amount omits the personal effects and jewelry.
questions.explanationJa:
配偶者以外との生存者権付き共有（JTWROS）の財産は、IRC §2040(a) により、生存者が購入資金を拠出したと証明できる部分を除き、全額が総遺産に含まれます。Wald が全額を負担しているので土地 $1,800,000 は全額算入され、身の回り品も §2033 により算入されます。
総遺産 = $150,000 + $1,800,000 = $1,950,000
$150,000 は土地を落とした額、$1,150,000 は土地の半分だけを算入した額で、これは配偶者間の共有（§2040(b)）の扱いです。$1,800,000 は身の回り品を落としています。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Property Taxation Q.32

questions.stem: Under the unified rate schedule,

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lifetime taxable gifts are taxed on a noncumulative basis.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Transfers at death are taxed on a noncumulative basis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lifetime taxable gifts and transfers at death are taxed on a cumulative basis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The gift tax rates are 5% higher than the estate tax rates.

questions.explanation:
The gift tax and estate tax share a single unified rate schedule (IRC §2001(c)), and both are computed cumulatively. Gift tax for a year is computed on all taxable gifts made in prior periods plus the current year, less the tax on prior gifts (§2502(a)). At death, adjusted taxable gifts are added to the taxable estate to compute the tentative estate tax (§2001(b)). Lifetime gifts and transfers at death are therefore taxed on a cumulative basis.
The statements that lifetime gifts or transfers at death are taxed on a noncumulative basis contradict this cumulative computation. Gift tax rates are not 5% higher than estate tax rates; the same rate schedule applies to both.
questions.explanationJa:
贈与税と遺産税は同一の統一税率表（IRC §2001(c)）を使い、どちらも累積ベースで計算します。各年の贈与税は過去分を含む累計の課税贈与に対する税額から過去分の税額を差し引いて求め（§2502(a)）、死亡時には調整課税贈与を課税遺産に加算して税額を計算します（§2001(b)）。
生前贈与や死亡時の移転を非累積で課税するという記述は誤りです。贈与税率が遺産税率より5%高いという事実もなく、同じ税率表が適用されます。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Property Taxation Q.33
